::: {#rem-invariant-parts}
#### The three parts of a loop invariant proof

A proof that an algorithm with one loop is correct (@def-correct-algorithm) usually names a statement $I$ and shows three things.

**Initialization.**
Assuming the precondition, $I$ is true at the first test of the guard.

**Maintenance.**
If $I$ and the guard are both true at a test, then $I$ is true at the next test.

**Termination.**
The loop stops, and when it stops, $I$ together with the guard being false implies the postcondition.

Initialization and maintenance are the two hypotheses of @thm-loop-invariant,
and they play the roles of the base case and the inductive step of a proof by induction (@def-proof-by-induction).
The theorem then says that $I$ is a loop invariant,
so the proof does not have to repeat the induction each time.
Termination is the part an induction proof does not have:
the theorem says what is true *if* the loop stops, not that it does.

:::
